subject: Cross-team launch commitments & risk stitching for QBR
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-14T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cross-team launch commitments & risk stitching for QBR

Team —

We're two weeks out from the QBR snapshot and I want one concise alignment thread that stitches launch commitments to active delivery risks. Goal: a single view I can present in the leadership readout showing what is on the critical path, who owns mitigations, and any customer-facing tradeoffs (ACME included).

High level asks:
- Can each owner confirm the current committed ship window for their surface and any slippage risk (ETA with confidence band)?
- For each risk, provide a one-line mitigation and the owner able to execute in the next 72 hours.
- Attachments: I've uploaded the current cadence matrix and our risk scan (see attached). Please update in-line or flag items that need escalation.

Files attached: launch_cadence_matrix.xlsx, prod-risk-scan.pdf

ACME — thanks for joining this thread. We'll surface any customer-impacting decisions; I'll flag anything that requires your sign-off.

Proposed timeline: final consolidated slide deck by EOD Tuesday (11/17). If any owner needs an earlier sync, call it out.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team launch commitments & risk stitching for QBR

On 11/14/26 08:12, Neha Kapoor wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We're two weeks out from the QBR snapshot...

Thanks — quick status from infra/runtime side:
- Committed window for model-serving infra: 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-10 (target deploy on 12/06). Confidence: 70% (we have a dependent CUDA kernel upgrade that landed late in validation).
- Key risk: kernel validation flicker under peak concurrent sessions. Mitigation: roll forward to patched kernel + conservative autoscale config. Owner: Vivek Kulkarni (will run targeted soak tests within 48 hours).
- Secondary risk: GPU capacity contention if Dedicated pools are consumed by burst traffic. Mitigation: pre-reserve burst pool for the week-of-launch and enable graceful fallback to smaller model variant for non-critical customers (requires product routing flag). Owner: Monica Patel to coordinate with Billing to temporary reserve capacity.

I'll update the cadence matrix with confidence bands after the soak tests. If we see regression in validation we'll propose a brief (~24–48 hr) delay to stabilize.

Vivek
VP, Engineering (Serving Runtime)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team launch commitments & risk stitching for QBR

Neha / Vivek —

Adding ops perspective and a couple of inline asks (see quoted notes). I've also placed comments in the Drive doc (link above).

Quoted notes:
> Key risk: kernel validation flicker under peak concurrent sessions.
- Ops note: when this occurs, error rates spike in <2 minutes. Our current HA playbooks will handle failover but we will see a customer latency impact if autoscale isn't tuned. Short mitigation: start canary in two smaller regions before global rollout to catch the flicker at lower blast radius. Owner: Irene Choi (will schedule the canary tomorrow morning).

> Secondary risk: GPU capacity contention...
- Ops ask: Monica — can you confirm whether temporary reservation can be executed via our Dedicated reservation API or requires procurement sign-off? If it needs procurement we'll need a pre-approved PO by EOD Monday to meet the week-of-launch reserve.

Proposed adjustment to timeline: keep the 12/06 deploy target but add a canary window 12/01–12/02 and a contingency rollback plan documented in the runbook. If owners agree I'll add the canary details to the slide export.

Irene
Director, Reliability Engineering
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-team launch commitments & risk stitching for QBR

Thanks all — good convergence. Summary / decisions (finalize these in cadence matrix and slide pack):
- Target deploy: 2026-12-06 (Confidence band: +2 / -1 days).
- Canary window: 2026-12-01 to 2026-12-02 (Owner: Irene Choi) — run in two smaller regions, validate kernel stability and autoscale behavior.
- Kernel validation mitigation: Vivek to execute patch soak tests within 48 hours and report pass/fail by 11/16 09:00 PST. If fail -> propose 24–48 hr slip and leadership ask.
- Capacity reservation: Monica to confirm whether we can reserve burst pool via API; if procurement required, Monica to surface PO request by 11/16 EOD.
- Customer-facing tradeoffs: enable fallback to smaller-model variant for non-critical traffic; Sarah, we'll include this in the customer decision matrix and notify impacted tenants during the canary.

Action items (owners and deadlines):
- Vivek: soak tests + update cadence matrix (11/16 09:00 PST)
- Irene: schedule canary + runbook update (start 12/01)
- Monica: capacity reservation decision + PO if needed (11/16 EOD)
- Neha: consolidate final slide for leadership (11/17 EOD)

Sarah — appreciate ACME's patience; please confirm whether your team needs a pre-canary tech review or if the customer notification cadence below works for you:
- Pre-canary tech review (optional): 11/20
- Customer notification: 11/29 (final runbook + expected impact)

Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
